vignettes.headline: Wendy asks twice for two different things
vignettes.body: Wendy sent a photo of you holding your grandfather's cat on his porch, maybe 1999, during what she calls your braids phase. You answered in seventeen minutes to say the cat was evil and you loved him. Eleven days earlier she asked whether to spend $135 on the radio thing, by Friday, because Rahul had to tell the guy. She also asked for headcount because you were the only one she didn't have an answer from and the table is a table. She added that she genuinely would not be weird about it either way. You answered in 5.6 days, after Friday, and said you were just seeing it.

vignettes.headline: Emergency in seventeen minutes, confirmation in eleven days
vignettes.body: Rosalind told you there was a problem and that she wanted you to hear it from her before Bea called. You answered in seventeen minutes, apologised, and asked to call at lunch instead of sending over a plan you'd only thought about for an hour. Three days later she told you that two weeks was the right answer, and that anyone who'd said one week would have been guessing. You answered in eleven days, after the feature was already live. The first message was a crisis she was managing for you. The second was her telling you that you were right.

vignettes.headline: Let me check and I'll ping you
vignettes.body: You have written "let me check" or "I'll ping" or "this week" fourteen times across nine people. Ten of those threads contain no further message from you. To Aiden it was "let me see when things calm down." To Josiah it was "give me a few days" about the intro. To Dane it was "fixing it this week" about something broken, and "will ping her this week" about something you were waiting to hear. Marguerite wrote back: "you have now told me twice that you will have a real answer after a conversation that has not yet been scheduled."

vignettes.headline: You slowed down first, then she did
vignettes.body: Your first two replies to Nkechi took three hours and five hours. Then 2.6 days. Then 3.6, then 6.6. She stayed steady at first: twenty hours, then 2.8 days. Then she stretched to ten days, then 9.4. Your messages got shorter as they got slower. You went from 167 words to 102 to 80 to 48 to eighteen. She wrote back on June 12th. That was eighteen days ago, and the thread is sitting on her. But you're the one who changed pace first, two days before she did.

vignettes.headline: Four questions you never got back to
vignettes.body: Josiah asked if you'd gotten a chance to think about the framing. Rosalind asked whether there was a way to see who changed an appointment. Karin asked you to send over what you had so far. Nkechi asked one more time in writing what happens if the seed doesn't close by the fall, and said she'd leave it after that. Four people, four threads, four questions that got no reply in that thread. The Josiah one was about a favor he'd explicitly said you could say no to. The Nkechi one she said she was asking for the last time.

vignettes.headline: You work a second shift after ten
vignettes.body: Seventy of your 91 messages went out during the day. Nineteen went out after 10pm, which over twelve weeks is more than one a week. Between 6pm and 10pm you sent one message total. That 12:47am note about billing and runway was five weeks ago. You wrote that you're not building for Rosalind, you're building something fifty clinics can use, and that he's selling a product that doesn't exist yet. You pointed out that billing the way he's describing it is six weeks. That message went out at 12:47am.
